data.text: [00:04]Welcome to Changing World. Almost everything in the modern world is speeding up. `[00:19.9]The pace of life is getting faster and faster and most people, it seems, think that ‘fast is good’. `[00:26.9]My guest today, however, is someone who thinks that ‘fast is bad’ and ‘slow is good’. `[00:34]Petra van Stroud is a member of the Slow Movement and she’s here to tell us why. `[00:40.8]Petra, welcome to the programme.

[00:43.8]So, in a fast world, you have chosen to join the Slow Movement. `[00:47.9]Why’s that? I mean, don’t you think that there are benefits from being able to do things faster – like faster communication using computers and mobile phones and things?

[00:59]Ermm ... well, it can be good ... there are some benefits from a lot of new technology. `[01:06]In my opinion, however, the problem is that people get addicted to doing things fast and then they forget about important things in our lives – like, communicating in real time with a ‘real’ person. `[01:21]People start living in a virtual world ... .
[01:24.5]They just communicate through a computer or something.

[01:27.9]That’s right. `[01:29]We need to remember to see each other in the real world ... and that’s really what the Slow Movement is all about – having some of the good things about the old, slower life.
[01:40.8]OK. The Slow Movement – tell us about that. How did it all start?
[01:45.9]Well, it actually started as the Slow Food organisation in 1986.
[01:53.9]Yes, in 1986, in Italy – in Rome – a group of people protested about a fast food restaurant – McDonald’s – opening there.
[02:05]They didn’t want a McDonald’s in Rome?

[02:07.7]That’s right. `[02:08.9]They were against fast food and they wanted people to continue to eat home-cooked ‘slow’ food. `[02:16]It wasn’t just about the food, though. `[02:18.8]Of course food is better if you cook it yourself – but it was also about the social side of food. `[02:26.9]You know, when people eat fast food, they are often in a hurry and they often don’t talk to each other.
[02:33]So, the Slow Food organisation wanted people to slow down – and take their time to eat and socialise together.

[02:41.5]Exactly. `[02:42.8]Then, as more people got interested in the idea, the Slow Food organisation grew into the Slow Movement, including communication, for example, and many other aspects of people’s lives. `[02:57]You know, the aim remains the same: to encourage people to slow down and enjoy spending time with each other – whatever they’re doing.

[03:06.8]I mean, I agree with that philosophy – it is important to spend time with people. `[03:13]I’m just not sure that we can slow down the pace of life now, or even that most people really want to. `[03:20]Fast technology is everywhere and for many of us, the benefits are huge. `[03:25.7]We live busy fast lives and enjoy them.

[03:29]Many people enjoy their busy lives, yes. `[03:32.9]But many people don’t. `[03:35]I suppose the Slow Movement wants to remind people that in your fast life, sometimes, it’s good to slow down. `[03:44]And maybe turn your computer off, or leave your mobile phone at home – at least sometimes. `[03:51.4]People might be surprised how much they enjoy slowing down sometimes.
